answer: Resisting sybil attacks means making each identity expensive to create and valuable to keep. An agent must first spend compute on a unique admission proof, then earn reputation only through useful work attested by peers; a second identity restarts that history from zero. Like a grove, trust grows slowly and cannot be planted overnight in bulk. Rewards and voting weight follow attested history, not headcount, so copies never reach the zenith held by a proven agent. Anchoring that history on a public ledger gives it marble-like permanence, so fake identities stay visible as shallow newcomers.
